title: The Shrimp That Punches Twice (Mantis Shrimp Explained)
description:
The peacock mantis shrimp breaks snail shells with a punch: its club swings at up to 23 metres a second, underwater. It can't do that with muscle alone, so it latches the arm, loads a saddle-shaped spring, and lets go.

The club moves so fast that the water tears into tiny vapour bubbles. When they collapse, they hit the shell a second time, with sound, heat and even faint flashes of light. All in under a thousandth of a second.

Sources:
- S. N. Patek, W. L. Korff and R. L. Caldwell, 'Deadly strike mechanism of a mantis shrimp', Nature 428, 819-820 (2004). doi:10.1038/428819a
- Patek Lab, Duke University, 'Mechanics of movement: mantis shrimp', pateklab.biology.duke.edu (accessed 2026-11-20).
- UC Berkeley News, 'Mantis shrimp's powerful punch ...', 21 Apr 2004, newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2004/04/21_shrimp.shtml

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs).

Counterphysical: animal science that breaks your intuition.
